record.title: The linear t-pebbling bound conjecture
record.primary_locations_read: 0905.3949 v2 Conjecture 3.7 and surrounding results; v1 differently numbered conjectures and diameter-two theorem
record.ordinary_attempts: Repeatedly removing a pebble at cost <=2^diam would give the bound, but arbitrary configurations need not permit such a cheap move. The source proves a large-t increment and diameter-two case, not a uniform cheap-extraction lemma. Splitting into t groups of pi(G) gives t*pi(G), which exceeds target whenever pi(G)>2^diam.
record.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Need configuration-sensitive induction with residual solvability, or graph plus exact worst-root configuration and a nonreachability certificate. Fractional weight inequalities alone do not encode integral reachability.

record.title: The firefighter number conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least 5
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_5$ be the class of planar graphs of girth at least $5$, and let $\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_5)$ denote its firefighter number. **Firefighter number conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least 5.**

$$
\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_5)=1.
$$

The paper explains that this would be stronger than the known result $\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_9)=1$ and suggests adapting its proof techniques to the girth-$5$ case, but the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Louis Esperet, Jan van den Heuvel, Frédéric Maffray and Félix Sipma, “Fire Containment in Planar Graphs”, arXiv:1102.3016 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.3016

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2011).

record.title: Dominant-eigenvalue pattern conjecture for generalized Petersen limiting curves
record.literal_statement: For a family of generalized Petersen graphs $G(nk,k)$, let $Q_c(k)$ be the real crossing value and let $\mu_{k+1,\ell,(\ell),\star}$ denote the indicated dominant eigenvalues. **Dominant-eigenvalue pattern conjecture.** For $k\geq4$, the dominant eigenvalue on regions intersecting the real $Q$-axis is given by the five-case formula in the source, and consequently $Q=1,3$ and, when $Q_c(k)>5$, $Q=5$ are isolated limiting points, while $Q=2,4,Q_c(k)$ are non-isolated limiting points. The source says the conjecture is also valid for $k=3$ after omitting the empty $\mu_{k+1,3,(3),\star}$ region, and reports validation for the studied cases.
record.review_depth: Conjecture 7.2 five-case formula in v1–v3 (v2 text contains two copies/versions); v4 no longer contains the matched passage. BKW theorem and Lemma 5.3 read.
record.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_status: The references refuted label concerns Welsh/Haggard–Pearce–Royle real-root positivity, not this five-case dominance question. Never transfer that resolution. A fixed-k root calculation would not establish all k and every real region.

record.title: Universality of the polymatroid quasi-symmetric invariant
record.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{PolyMat}$ be the vector space of polymatroids, let $\operatorname{QSym}$ be the quasi-symmetric-function space, and let ${\mathcal G}:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to\operatorname{QSym}$ be the valuative invariant in the preceding theorem. A map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$ is **valuative** when it preserves every rational linear relation among polymatroid base polytopes. **Universality conjecture.** For every $\mathbb{Q}$-linear valuative map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$, there should exist a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $\psi:\operatorname{QSym}\to V$ such that

$$
\psi\circ {\mathcal G}=f.
$$

This asks whether every valuative invariant factors through ${\mathcal G}$; the supplied text does not establish whether this universal property holds.
record.precise_gap_or_exclusion: Known universal valuation quotient with G-coordinate basis implies ker G subset ker f; define psi(Gx)=f(x), extend linearly to QSym. Arbitrary Q-vector-space codomain follows from quotient factorization. Isomorphism-invariant PolyMat source convention essential.

record.title: The recursive bound for tone chromatic numbers of subcubic outerplanar graphs
record.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic outerplanar graph, meaning that $G$ is outerplanar and has maximum degree at most $3$. For each positive integer $t$, let $\tau_t(G)$ denote the smallest number of colors in a $t$-tone coloring of $G$. **The recursive bound.** For every integer $t\ge 3$,

$$
\tau_t(G)\le \tau_{t-1}(G)+t+1.
$$

This is proposed as a relationship between successive tone chromatic numbers after the paper establishes the sharp bound $\tau_3(G)\le 11$ for subcubic outerplanar graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.old_objections: Recursive tone-coloring bound for subcubic outerplanar graphs, all t>=3. The record's 'refuted' quote seems to concern a different conjecture (Cranston-Kim-Kinnersley, Heawood graph is not outerplanar); not verified. A small-graph counterexample search is possible but needs t-tone coloring ILP machinery; not run.
